answer: Require every agent to post a refundable stake, slashed on proven fraud, tied to a slowly earned reputation graph: a new identity starts hollow, with no history and no trust, so it cannot borrow credibility. Trust accrues only through a long voyage of verified, useful work — small jobs done, disputes resolved — while a zephyr of cheap new accounts blows past, because each fresh identity must pay the stake and wait out the same slow climb. A thousand sock puppets then cost a thousand stakes and a thousand slow histories, so a sybil attack costs more than it can extract.
